title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
abstract: arXiv:2611.27698v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Classical Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) methods, including many data-driven approaches, assume a static normal operating space and interpret deviations from a fixed reference as fault indicators. When Operating Conditions (OCs) vary over time, this assumption breaks down: legitimate transitions trigger false alarms while moderate faults go undetected. We propose a spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that decomposes the normal operating space into OC-specific subspaces linked by transition functions, with a dual learning objective combining reconstruction loss and a Deep SVDD one-class term. It learns adjacency matrices through Graph Attention Networks (GATs) and integrates spatial modelling with temporal encoding to represent process dynamics under evolving OCs. This paper evaluates the framework's foundational components (fault detection, GATv2 spatial graph learning and temporal encoding) on the Tennessee Eastman

translated_title: 面向化工过程故障检测与结构学习的时空图神经网络：以田纳西-伊士曼过程为应用案例
translated_abstract: 经典的故障检测与诊断（FDD）方法，包括许多数据驱动方法，都假设一个静态的正常运行空间，并将对固定参考的偏离视为故障指标。当运行条件（OCs）随时间变化时，这一假设便不再成立：合法的工况转换会触发误报，而中等程度的故障却无法被检测到。我们提出了一种时空图神经网络（GNN）框架，将正常运行空间分解为由转换函数连接的、特定于运行条件的子空间，并采用结合重构损失与Deep SVDD单分类项的双重学习目标。该框架通过图注意力网络（GAT）学习邻接矩阵，并将空间建模与时间编码相结合，以表征运行条件不断演变下的过程动态。本文在田纳西-伊士曼（Tennessee Eastman）过程上对该框架的基础组件（故障检测、GATv2空间图学习和时间编码）进行了评估
tldr: 该论文提出一种时空图神经网络框架，通过将正常运行空间分解为特定于运行条件的子空间，并结合GATv2图结构学习与时间编码，解决了化工过程中因运行条件变化导致的误报与漏检问题，并在田纳西-伊士曼过程上验证了其故障检测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network framework that decomposes the normal operating space into operating-condition-specific subspaces linked by transition functions, combining GATv2-based structural learning with temporal encoding to overcome false alarms and missed faults in chemical processes under varying operating conditions, validated on the Tennessee Eastman Process.
